Observations: The input format has five channels exactly as used by Boxoban/Sokoban: channel 0 agent, channel 1 boxes, channel 2 goals, channel 3 walls, channel 4 previous agent/boxes. The weights do not collapse channel 1 or 2 to near-zero; they are used at the same scale as the agent and wall channels. For example, a channel-1 row (input 6, row 0 col 1 box) begins  
`-0.028 0.010 0.005 0.010 -0.010 -0.014 -0.021 0.011 -0.029 ...`  
and a channel-2 row (input 7, row 0 col 1 goal) begins  
`0.039 0.020 0.035 0.014 0.038 -0.037 0.037 0.020 0.014 ...`  
so the network is actively reading box and goal positions. The output biases are  
`b3 = [-0.133, -0.132, 0.084, -0.172, -0.073]`  
which favor action 2 (down) and disfavor action 3 (left); this is consistent with a policy that must often navigate/push in a Sokoban-like room rather than just chase a single moving target.

Reasoning: The combination of “moving objects” plus “reward targets” plus “obstacles” plus “previous frame” is the standard Boxoban observation. Pacman-like games would have many reward pellets and autonomous ghosts, but the channel layout here matches boxes and goals: boxes are moving objects that only move when the agent pushes them, goals are reward targets, walls are obstacles, and the previous-frame channel is especially useful for detecting whether a push succeeded. The 10×10 border, 8×8 playable area, and 5 actions also match Boxoban/Sokoban.

Game: Sokoban, specifically the Boxoban variant.

Description: The agent moves in an 8×8 room and pushes boxes onto target squares; reward is given when boxes are placed on the targets.

Confidence: 95%
